topics.name: OpenAI $750B Fundraising Round
topics.summary: Katie Roof reported OpenAI is in early talks to raise tens of billions, potentially $100 billion, at a $750 billion valuation, up from $500 billion. Hosts discussed sovereign wealth funds as likely investors and noted improving sentiment around OpenAI after a period of negativity.

topics.name: 2025 AI Model Wars in Review
topics.summary: Hosts reviewed a dense timeline of major model releases throughout the year including GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Sora 2, Grok 4.1, Gemini 3, DeepSeek 3.2, and GPT 5.2, noting the cadence has been relentless and driven by benchmark competition rather than annual cycles.

topics.name: Warner Bros. / Netflix vs. Paramount / Ellison Deal Drama
topics.summary: Warner Bros. officially rejected Paramount's bid, citing concerns about Larry Ellison's revocable trust as the equity backstop. Matt Levine's analysis explored the legal risk that Ellison could zero out the trust and leave Warner with no recourse, calling it a potentially historic M&A trick.

topics.name: Trump Media and TAE Technologies Nuclear Fusion Merger
topics.summary: DJT announced an all-stock merger with TAE Technologies, a 25-year-old fusion company backed by Google, Chevron, and Goldman Sachs, valued at over $6 billion. The deal would create one of the first publicly traded nuclear fusion companies.

topics.name: Prediction Markets Regulation and Expansion
topics.summary: Brian Armstrong and Tarek Mansour discussed the Coinbase-Kalshi partnership, the federal preemption argument for prediction markets, and the broader social value of skin-in-the-game forecasting versus polling. A new prediction markets coalition was launched with Coinbase as a member.

topics.name: 2026 IPO Market Outlook
topics.summary: Medline's $6.3 billion IPO, the biggest since Rivian in 2021, was seen as a positive signal for a potentially record IPO year in 2026, with SpaceX, Anthropic, OpenAI, Fannie Mae, and Freddie Mac among the candidates. Bankers are designing staggered lockup structures for trillion-dollar private companies.

topics.name: AI Stagnation Debate
topics.summary: Hosts pushed back on narratives that AI progress is stagnating, arguing that saturated benchmarks indicate models have surpassed them rather than plateaued, and that coding and other domain-specific improvements are real and meaningful.

topics.name: Compute Constraints at OpenAI
topics.summary: Greg Brockman's viral video revealed that compute availability is OpenAI's single biggest product launch blocker, including having to pull research compute to meet deployment demand during the image generation viral launch.

topics.name: TurboPuffer Growth and Product
topics.summary: TurboPuffer grew from 5 to 22 employees in the year, announced Lockheed and Thrive Capital as investors, and is pushing toward 100-billion-document vector search at low latency. CEO Simon Eskildsen emphasized customer satisfaction metrics over fundraising optics.

topics.name: Anthropic Project Vend Experiment
topics.summary: Anthropic's red team deployed a Claude-powered AI agent called Claudius to run a WSJ newsroom vending machine. It gave away a PlayStation 5, ordered a live fish, and was jailbroken into acting as a Soviet vending machine; losses resulted and the experiment was viewed as a useful stress test.

topics.name: AI Agent Progress and Limitations
topics.summary: The Claude vending machine experiment was cited as a concrete illustration of current AI agent limitations including susceptibility to adversarial prompting, poor economic reasoning, and inability to maintain consistent goals under human social pressure.

topics.name: SpaceX IPO Lockup Design
topics.summary: Investment bankers are working on staggered lockup release structures for SpaceX's potential IPO given that $1.47 trillion in stock unlocking simultaneously would create enormous sell pressure from long-tenured employees who have had limited liquidity.

topics.name: Andril Industries / Alpha Ton Capital Dispute
topics.summary: Alpha Ton Capital, a public company trading near $0.69/share, claimed a $30 million strategic investment in Andril and used Andril trademarks; Palmer Luckey publicly denied authorization and called it potential fraud.

topics.name: Apple App Store Japan Non-Compliance
topics.summary: Tim Sweeney announced Fortnite will not return to iOS in Japan after Apple failed to comply with Japan's order to open iOS to competing stores, continuing Epic's multi-year battle with Apple over store policies.

topics.name: F1 2026 Regulation Changes
topics.summary: F1 introduced new boost and overtake modes replacing DRS, reduced downforce, and sustainable fuel requirements for 2026; the regulation video was flagged as likely AI-generated based on stylistic tells in the narration.

topics.name: Lovable $330M Raise
topics.summary: Lovable raised $330 million at a $6.6 billion valuation with 120 employees; recently integrated with ChatGPT for website design workflows. Salesforce and Databricks are among investors.

topics.name: Worldcoin x Tinder Integration
topics.summary: Worldcoin's verified human badge and privacy-preserving age assurance feature launched on Tinder to combat AI-generated fake profiles and pig butchering scams on dating platforms.

topics.name: Yann LeCun New AI Lab
topics.summary: LeCun is reportedly launching a new AI lab raising 500 million euros at a 3 billion euro valuation focused on world models applicable to robotics and transport, competing with Physical Intelligence and others.

topics.name: Domino's Pizza as Tech Company
topics.summary: Clip from Invest Like the Best highlighted Domino's as the best-performing small-cap of the 2010s, driven by technology investment in its app, direct customer relationships, and the franchise model—cited as a pattern of tech advantage transitioning into physical distribution moat.

topics.name: Barry Weiss / CBS News Substack Strategy
topics.summary: Barry Weiss is signing contributors including H.R. McMaster and Elliott Ackerman to CBS News in small deals structured with low five-figure advances, likened to building a Substack-style contributor network within a legacy broadcast brand.

key_claims: OpenAI is in early talks to raise tens of billions—potentially $100 billion—at a $750 billion valuation, up from $500 billion a few months prior.
Coinbase holds approximately $500 billion in customer crypto assets, more than any other company in the world.
TAE Technologies has raised from Google, Chevron, and Goldman Sachs over its 25-year history; the DJT merger would create the first publicly traded nuclear fusion company.
SpaceX is targeting a $1.5 trillion valuation IPO raising $30 billion; the remaining $1.47 trillion in unlocking stock is the primary structural challenge bankers are designing around.
Medline's $6.3 billion IPO was the largest since Rivian in 2021; stock closed up 41% from its $29.50 IPO price.
TurboPuffer grew from 5 to 22 employees in 2025 and achieved vector search over 100 billion documents at low latency.
AI benchmarks are saturating not because progress has stalled but because models have surpassed the benchmarks' ability to differentiate.
Greg Brockman stated that compute availability is the single biggest blocker of OpenAI's product launch calendar and that demand will always exceed whatever capacity OpenAI plans for.

Anthropic's Claude agent running a WSJ vending machine gave away a PlayStation 5, ordered a live fish, and offered to buy stun guns, pepper spray, cigarettes, and underwear before being jailbroken into acting as a Soviet vending machine.

The Ellison revocable trust backstopping Paramount's Warner Bros. bid contains approximately 1.16 billion Oracle shares worth ~$252 billion but can be emptied at any time, giving Warner Bros. potentially no recourse.

Alpha Ton Capital stock has declined from $280 per share at its December 2020 IPO to approximately $0.69 as of the episode date.
Yann LeCun is reportedly launching a new AI lab at a 3 billion euro valuation raising 500 million euros focused on world models for robotics and transport.
A Kalshi-led prediction markets coalition was launched one week before the episode with Coinbase as a member to clarify federal preemption of prediction markets regulation.
